body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-17 on a ticket-only PR (#420), which is what makes it unambiguous: the branch
changed no code, so the failure cannot be a regression from content. Main was green on every recent
run. The gate went red on Windows alone.

MEASURED, both directions, before blaming anything:
- The failing case is `ArchiveBackend purge sweeps files, not id-by-fan > removes canonical files and
  stragglers across many ids in one pass, counting distinct ids` (test/store/archive.test.ts:171).
- Windows: the FILE took 22317ms for 8 tests and that one case hit the 20000ms per-test ceiling.
- Linux, same commit: the same case runs in **511ms**. Every other test in the file is single-digit ms.
- A ~40x platform multiplier on roughly 250 file operations (200 appends with fsync, 50 straggler
  copies) plus 250 signatures.

THE DEFENDER HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, and this matters because it is the obvious suspect. CI excludes
the workspace and temp dir from Defender's real-time scan, best-effort with a try/catch, so a runner
that refuses the call pays the scan tax invisibly. The log for the failing run shows BOTH exclusions
succeeding (`excluded D:\a\loam\loam`, `excluded D:\a\_temp`). The cost is Windows file creation and
fsync on a loaded runner, not an unprotected scan.

HISTORY, so the next reader does not re-derive it: T155 pooled the archive's fsyncs at width 16 after
this file measured 12-14s on Windows against 0.7s on Linux. T159 then raised 32 files from a
self-imposed 15s to the platform-informed 20s default, citing this very file at 20.1s. So this case
has been at the edge twice and has now crossed it a third time. Raising the ceiling again is the move
that has already been made twice.

THE DIAGNOSIS: a RAIL weight problem, not a spec-accuracy one. The property under test is that purge
sweeps FILES rather than walking id-by-fan, and that it counts DISTINCT IDS ACTUALLY FOUND. Three
populations carry that proof — canonical files with a crash-left `.tmp` straggler beside them,
canonical files alone, and ids that were never present (the already-swept case a retry produces). The
RATIOS are load-bearing. The MAGNITUDE is not: nothing in the test asserts a duration or a pass count,
so 200 deltas prove exactly what 60 prove, at a third of the Windows cost.

THE FIX: shrink the fixture, keeping every population and every ratio. 200 appended becomes 60; 100
doomed becomes 30; 50 with stragglers becomes 15; 50 never-present becomes 15; the expected removed
count and the surviving count follow. Do NOT raise a timeout, and do NOT widen an assertion — both
delete the rail while appearing to repair it.

COST, known up front: test/store/archive.test.ts is FROZEN by T67. This is an authorization pair in
scripts/rail-renames.json and therefore two PRs — land the pairs, then the edit. Generate the pairs
FROM the diff so the two agree by construction, and verify the gate answers EXEMPT against a
synthetic base before pushing.

PROVE THE SHRUNK FIXTURE STILL BITES, and this is the part that must not be skipped. Probe both
directions against the smaller numbers: (a) make purge count REQUESTED ids rather than ids it found —
the expected count must go red; (b) make purge skip `.tmp` stragglers — the directory sweep must go
red. A fixture reduction that stops catching either is a rail deletion wearing a performance fix's
clothes.

WHY IT OUTRANKS THE QUEUE: main is protected and requires the Windows gate. An intermittently red
archive test makes every merge in the repo a coin flip, and trains whoever sees it to re-run instead of
investigate — which is the whole harm the standing flake rule names.

OVERTAKEN (stale sweep, 2026-08-25): PR #422 (commit 31c6e1d), under authorization PR #421, shrank the purge-sweep fixture exactly as the ticket prescribed: main's test/store/archive.test.ts now appends 60 deltas, dooms 30, plants 15 stragglers, requests 15 never-present ids, and asserts removed === 30, with both red-probes recorded in the commit message.
title: archive.test.ts's purge sweep exceeds the 20s budget on Windows — 250 file ops to prove a counting property
